title: Chosen Cartesian lifts detect preservation of all Cartesian edges
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, quasicategories, equivalence edges, functor quasicategories, and homotopy categories of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], Cartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and relative natural markings of [lem-coef-relative-marked-anodyne-calculus]. Fix $n\geq0$ and a small Cartesian fibration $p:Y\to\Delta^n$. For each $0\leq j\leq n$ choose a set $B_j$ of vertices of $Y_j$ such that every vertex of $Y_j$ is equivalent within $Y_j$ to a vertex in $B_j$. For every $b\in B_j$ and $i\leq j$, choose a $p$-Cartesian edge $e_{i,j,b}:c_{i,j,b}\to b$ over the edge $i\to j$, with $c_{i,j,b}\in Y_i$.

Every $p$-Cartesian edge $d:x\to y$ over $i\to j$ admits $b\in B_j$, equivalences $u:c_{i,j,b}\to x$ in $Y_i$ and $v:b\to y$ in $Y_j$, and an equality $[d][u]=[v][e_{i,j,b}]$ in $hY$. Cartesianity is preserved and reflected by precomposition or postcomposition with equivalences in the corresponding vertex fibers, using any triangle composite. For any other small Cartesian fibration $Z\to\Delta^n$ and any simplicial map $f:Y\to Z$ over the base, $f$ preserves every Cartesian edge if and only if each $f(e_{i,j,b})$ is Cartesian. This preservation property is invariant under coherent natural equivalence between functors over $\Delta^n$. The assertions include $n=0$ and empty fibers; no global choice of a nonempty fiber is assumed.
